scope: Isolated SQL kernels over captured production facts; no engine cutover or full-rule/full-repository speed claim.

host.allocator: Rust default system allocator; engine addon not loaded

method: Six fresh serial trials per variant, rotated order. Small correctness control uses three.
Each trial has a 20-second subprocess timeout. Every controller has a 115-second deadline and stops work at 112 seconds.
Exact sorted result multisets, including repeated rows and witness identities, match across all variants and trials.
CPU uses getrusage user plus system time. Kernel includes SQL generation, variant setup/indexing, preparation, execution, counters and result collection.
Common typed fact copy and both indexes are reported separately and included in totalKernelCpuMs.
Database copying, input shape checks, open/configure, output sorting/serialization, and EXPLAIN diagnostics are outside totalKernelCpuMs. Individual counters retain copy and input-check CPU.
Batch kernels use common lab facts for consistency, although decoding does not consume that extra copy. Those totals are not a production setup estimate.
Peak RSS covers the fresh child process, including parity result storage and diagnostic preparation. It is not engine peak RSS.
tempBytes counts allocated temp-schema pages at completion, including free pages. It excludes transient CTE spools, journal/WAL and total disk high water.
Small CPU measurements remain noisy. CV and every sample are retained; matched trials were added after initial variation exceeded five percent.

decisions.range: Proceed to a production lowering only for proven preorder forests. Restrict roots first; retain intervals instead of pairs. Preserve generic graph recursion and selected-edge semantics.
decisions.demand: Proceed with explicit demand-key cuts before costly native predicates. The syntax-only selective query still decodes all identifiers. No whole-job gain established; total setup-inclusive selective and cut samples overlap.
decisions.utility: Share semantic definitions across the policy and reuse existing physical cuts. Named MATERIALIZED CTEs alone still show preparation expansion. The depth stress is synthetic and does not establish a production rule speedup.
decisions.batch: Keep current streaming node table for CPU execution. Reject extra copied column buffers as a CPU optimization. Retain immutable descriptor and bounded-wave requirements for future GPU producers; no GPU speed measured.

semanticLimits: Range kernel models the authored state root expansion guard, but uses numeric captured CST identities and a selected count/first-witness consumer. It is not the full authored state stage with string IDs.
Demand kernel implements removed-calls with default all entryPoint. The primary source is clean for that predicate. A fixture supplies a positive, a clean file and wrong-field rejection.
Utility stress uses distinct modulo-filter consumers of shared syntax-key relations. It does not implement capture scope, parameterized utilities, recursion or outcome semantics.
Batch prototype implements one structural terminal over file/range descriptors. It does not implement a full file/program grid, GPU launches, device residence, work budgets or cancellation.
Fixture parity and kernel row equality do not cover ordered choice, negative captures, unknown/failure outcomes or the complete ported suite.
batch.waves counts bounded CPU decode chunks. Future GPU launch count follows terminal dependencies rather than files, roots or these chunks.
